solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: May upset with Times covering resistance by Conservative? That's irregular

indicators.note: by means placed next to, so the Conservative abbreviation follows
covering means the jumbled letters wrap around the symbol for resistance
upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters of May and Times are rearranged together

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A comment that Theresa May shrugging off The Times with Tory resistance behind her is a strange state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: May is the former Prime Minister and The Times a newspaper in the surface, but both are just anagram fodder here; 'upset' jumbles them, 'covering' wraps the result round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking symmetry is uneven or irregular in shape or arrangement.

clue.text: Xhosan desert has plenty of this

definitions.text: Xhosan desert has plenty of this

indicators.note: has means the words contain the answer within them, spanning the end of one and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A remark that a desert in Xhosa country is full of a certain substance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the letters sit across 'Xhosan desert', and deserts are famously full of the stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserts are largely made of fine grains of rock, the obvious thing they hold in abundance.

clue.text: Writing about a time in service

indicators.note: about means the letters for writing go around the rest

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something written about a moment during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the morning prayer service of the Anglican church and the night office in monastic tradition.

clue.text: IT scale could be flexible

indicators.note: could be means these letters might become something else when reordered

explanation.surface: A claim that an information-technology scale might be adaptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stretches and springs back is pliant, the same idea as flexible.

clue.text: Check area lacking energy in two parts?

indicators.note: lacking means the letters for energy are taken out of the word for area
in two parts tells us the removed letters are not side by side but split up within the longer word

parts.note: a region is an area
go means energy or drive, as in full of go

explanation.surface: Checking whether a zone without power has been split in two.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking G and O, which are separated, out of REGION leaves R, E, I, N.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain or curb, which is what check means as a verb.

clue.text: Hover about in outskirts of Camden to find sign of rank

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the outer letters
outskirts of means only the edge letters of the word are used
about means the letters of hover are moved around

explanation.surface: A drone hovering on the edge of a London district in search of a military badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns HOVER into HEVRO, which goes 'in' C and N, the outskirts of Camden, a district of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: A V-shaped stripe on a sleeve shows a non-commissioned officer's rank, such as sergeant or corporal.

clue.text: Masculine female player? That's criminal!

parts.note: male means masculine
an actor is a player on the stage

explanation.surface: A man who plays a woman's part on stage is condemned as an offender.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer, especially one who breaks the law, is a criminal.

clue.text: Nerve poison? It could be true in Oxon

indicators.note: could be means the letters of the phrase might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a rumour is true in Oxfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxon is the short name for Oxfordshire, the English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that damages or disrupts nerve tissue is a poison acting on the nervous system.

clue.text: Spread most of plaster regularly on end of tile

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped from what is picked
regularly means every other letter is taken from the word
end of means only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Instructions for applying plaster evenly onto the edge of a tile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes P, A, T, R from plaster; 'most of' drops the R; the end of tile adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth paste of liver or meat is something you spread on toast.

clue.text: First step of independent resident around Italian island

indicators.note: around means the word for resident goes round the other letters

parts.note: a native is a resident of a place
IT is a common abbreviation for Italian, as in vermouth

explanation.surface: A local politician leads the way around an Italian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the opening move in an undertaking is taking the first step.

clue.text: Silly revenge? Not good to show superficial refinement

indicators.note: silly means foolish or mixed up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not means the letter for good is left out

explanation.surface: Pointless retaliation done without virtue only gives a thin appearance of class.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin decorative layer over cheaper wood gives the figurative sense of a polished surface hiding something lesser.

clue.text: Tips secretary over into pool of dirty water

indicators.note: over means the whole run of letters is turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written; that the answer also runs backwards through the full letters of these words is a coincidence of the charade, not a hiding device

explanation.surface: An assistant gets tipped headfirst into a filthy pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit for sewage or waste water is a foul pool of dirty water.

clue.text: Plan stratagem to seize Eastern booze

parts.note: a chart is a plan or map

indicators.note: to seize means the word for stratagem grabs the letter and holds it inside

parts.note: a ruse is a stratagem or trick

explanation.surface: A scheme to grab alcohol from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A green or yellow French herbal liqueur, made by monks, is a type of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Drinks containing malt liquor for loyalists

indicators.note: containing means the word for drinks holds the other word inside

parts.note: sups means drinks, takes small mouthfuls
porter is a dark beer brewed from malt

explanation.surface: Pints of dark beer handed out to the faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: People who back a cause or team faithfully are its loyal followers.

clue.text: Innards of automaton upgraded to 100mph

indicators.note: innards of means the letters come from inside the run of words, across the join

explanation.surface: A robot's insides are improved so it can reach a hundred miles an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: A ton is British slang for 100, so doing a ton-up means riding at 100mph, a motorcyclist's term.
explanation.definitionFit: Ton-up is British slang for reaching a hundred miles per hour, especially on a motorbike.

clue.text: Hibernating dung beetle joins male insect

parts.note: a dor is a kind of dung beetle, a crossword favourite
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A sleeping dung beetle teams up with a male bug.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal sleeping through winter is inactive, the state described as lying asleep or quiet.

clue.text: Party, Republican, vacated ministers' sleeping quarters

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the inner letters are removed leaving only the outside ones

explanation.surface: A Republican gathering clears out the politicians' bedrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Shared bedrooms in a college or hostel are dormitories, places to sleep.

clue.text: Depression touching large intestine

parts.note: a col is a dip or low point between two peaks
on means touching, in contact with

explanation.surface: Feeling low has an effect on the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: The main part of the large bowel, between caecum and rectum, is a section of the gut.

clue.text: They might bite — or sting when weight's added

indicators.note: added works in reverse: putting the letter for weight onto the answer gives the stinging insects, so take it away

parts.note: wasps are insects that sting

explanation.surface: A warning about creatures that might bite, or sting if they get heavier.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue backwards: the answer plus W makes WASPS, insects that sting, so WASPS minus W is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: These venomous snakes, like Cleopatra's, are known for their deadly bite.

clue.text: Adheres they say to hateful river

indicators.note: they say means the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: sticks means adheres

explanation.surface: Something clings to an odious stream, or so people report.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the underworld river's name derives from the Greek for hatred.

clue.text: Pair join medic in Italian cathedral

parts.note: a duo is a pair
MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: Two people meet a doctor in a church in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word for a city's principal church, as in Florence.

clue.text: Drunk medics imbibing European wine

indicators.note: imbibing means taking in, so the jumbled letters swallow the letter
drunk means intoxicated and so jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tipsy doctors drinking a continental vintage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges MEDICS as DEMISC; 'imbibing' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium-sweet champagne or sparkling style is a type of wine.

clue.text: Musical drama starts to translate Elgar work

parts.note: an opera is a drama set to music

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A sung stage piece begins to render an Elgar composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like a noun after Elgar but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To function or run, as a machine does, is to work.

clue.text: After tango, we spot unusual dance

indicators.note: after means the anagram comes following the letter for tango

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are arranged in an odd new way

explanation.surface: Following a tango, someone notices a strange dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom dance in quick march time is a named type of dance.

clue.text: Special gold covered pouch

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
ran means covered, as in ran a distance

explanation.surface: A unique pouch with a gold lining.
explanation.walkthrough: A sporran is the pouch worn at the front of a Scottish kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The fur or leather purse hung in front of a kilt is a pouch.

clue.text: Top up that could make judge poorly

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a judge in sport
ill means poorly, unwell

explanation.surface: A further dose of medicine that might make a magistrate sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Filling a glass again is topping it up.

clue.text: Turkish ambassador's welcomed by Roosevelt, chillingly

indicators.note: welcomed by means held inside the following words, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A president greets an envoy from Turkey coldly.
explanation.definitionFit: An obscure word, from the Turkish, for an ambassador or envoy.

clue.text: Enlarge animal park before first of March

indicators.note: before means the park comes ahead of the letter in the answer

parts.note: a zoo is an animal park

indicators.note: first of means just the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Expanding the zoo ahead of the start of March.
explanation.definitionFit: To magnify an image with a camera lens is to make it look bigger.

clue.text: Ivan (the) Terrible is self-complacent

indicators.note: terrible means awful, so the letters are put into a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Ivan the Terrible was full of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' is part of the Russian tsar's title but acts as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being conceited and pleased with oneself is being smug or self-satisfied.

clue.text: Scattered cold air almost spat. Exactly!

definitions.text: Scattered cold air almost spat. Exactly!

indicators.note: scattered means spread about, so the letters are thrown into a new order
almost means the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Bursts of cold air and a near-spat, here and there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims spat to SPA, and 'Scattered' mixes that with COLD AIR; the whole clue also describes the answer, as 'Exactly!' hints.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring now and then, at scattered intervals, is the meaning of the rarer form of sporadic.

clue.text: Use small boat to reach Channel island

parts.note: an ark is a boat, like Noah's

explanation.surface: Taking a little boat to get to an island in the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A small car-free island near Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands.

clue.text: Exercise lines in Advent can be persuasive

indicators.note: in means the letters go inside the word for advent

parts.note: advent means arrival, a coming
PE is physical education, exercise
L is short for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Gym work done during the run-up to Christmas wins people over.
explanation.walkthrough: Advent here is not the Christmas season but its plain sense of an arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument that cannot be resisted is forceful and convincing.
